checkedAlternates.risk: Ducks walk on land and fly, so they fit the land-bird group on a loose reading.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The distinguishing behaviour is swimming; the three-item row is exactly the birds that both fly and swim.

checkedAlternates.risk: Same as the duck: swans fly long distances.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Swans are water birds, and moving one out leaves the flying-and-swimming row short.

checkedAlternates.risk: A player who has never seen an emu may assume it flies.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Emus are flightless. This is the one knowledge dependency in the puzzle; the ostrich beside it should carry the group.

checkedAlternates.risk: Owls hunt near water in some regions.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Owls do not swim, and the land-flier row is four items with no room to lose one.

authorReview.notes: Overlaps the Animal Movement family released 2026-09-27 in dimension but not in items; birds are narrow enough that the rule reads differently.

blindPlaytest.notes: Watch the emu for recognition, not for ambiguity. If it is unfamiliar, swap it for a cassowary only if that is better known in the test group, otherwise use a kiwi.
